issues.summary: Atomic 409 rejects the whole batch when any Safe is deployed
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: The PR description says the atomic rejection is intended and matches the endpoint's existing 409 on param collisions. The claimed comparison is also false: the space endpoint (space-counterfactual-safes.controller.ts:55) only has @Get, and filterUndeployed filters reads, not writes.

issues.summary: E2E POST tests pass only via the fail-open path; the deployed→409 and confirmed-undeployed paths are never exercised end to end
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: createTestModule swaps in TestNetworkModule, where networkService.get is a bare vi.fn() (test.network.module.ts). The e2e spec never stubs it, so isSafe/getApi throws and assertNoneDeployed (counterfactual-safes.service.ts:90) returns false. The service unit tests do cover the 409 logic, so the gap is mostly in wiring coverage.

issues.summary: The fail-open catch swallows errors without logging
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: counterfactual-safes.service.ts:90 has a bare `catch { return false; }`, so the guard can be silently disabled, for example on an unsupported chain or a zod parse failure. Other fail-open paths in the repo log with loggingService.warn (safe.repository.ts:395). This is an observability gap, not a functional defect.

issues.label: low
issues.evidence: counterfactual-safes.service.ts:83-92 is nearly identical to space-counterfactual-safes.service.ts:63-74. Any policy change (logging, allSettled) would have to be made in two places or GET and POST could drift apart.

issues.summary: The new 409 response is not documented in Swagger
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: counterfactual-safes.controller.ts:57-62 documents only 201 and 401, while members.controller.ts and address-book-requests.controller.ts use @ApiConflictResponse. The existing collision 409 was also undocumented, but the PR adds a new 409 case without documenting it.

issues.summary: Up to 100 concurrent isSafe lookups per POST with no concurrency limit
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: The schema caps the batch at .max(100) (counterfactual-safe.dto.entity.ts:29), and Promise.all fires all lookups at once. They go through the cached transaction API, and 100 is bounded, so the impact is modest.

issues.summary: The unit test mock ignores chainId, so passing the wrong chainId would go undetected
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: counterfactual-safes.service.spec.ts uses `mockImplementation(async ({ address }) => address === deployed.address)`, and no test asserts isSafe was called with the correct chainId. That is a small, real hole in the test.

issues.summary: The test builds the DTO by hand instead of using a shared builder
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: createDto in counterfactual-safes.service.spec.ts:22-44 maps 14 fields by hand. It is a style and maintainability preference with no current defect.

issues.summary: Duplicate (chainId, address) entries in a batch trigger redundant isSafe calls
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: Duplicates in one batch are unlikely, and isSafe goes through a cache-first datasource, so the extra cost is negligible.

issues.summary: isSafe calls cannot be aborted once one Safe is found deployed
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: This is a micro-optimization. Promise.all waiting for the remaining cached lookups has no meaningful cost.

issues.summary: The comment describes what the code does rather than why
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: The comment at counterfactual-safes.service.ts:78-79 is two short lines and already states the fail-open policy. This is purely stylistic.

issues.summary: The space GET response may omit chains whose Safes were all filtered out
issues.label: unverifiable
issues.evidence: This concerns space-counterfactual-safes.service.ts from the earlier PR (#3247), not lines changed here. Whether clients rely on empty per-chain arrays can't be settled from this codebase.
